title: Financial Fraud Detection Using Value At Risk With Machine Learning In Skewed Data
abstract: Financial fraud has become a major challenge for banking and financial institutions due to the rapid growth of digital transactions and online payment systems. Detecting fraudulent activities is particularly difficult when transaction datasets are highly imbalanced or skewed, where legitimate transactions significantly outnumber fraudulent ones. Traditional rule-based systems often fail to identify complex and evolving fraud patterns, making it necessary to adopt intelligent data-driven approaches. This study presents a machine learning-based financial fraud detection framework that incorporates the concept of Value at Risk (VaR) to improve the identification of suspicious transactions in skewed datasets. The proposed approach utilizes VaR as a financial risk indicator to estimate potential losses in transaction amounts and integrate it as an additional feature in the fraud detection process. By combining risk-based financial analysis with machine learning techniques, the system is able to capture abnormal transaction behaviors more effectively. The dataset undergoes preprocessing steps including data cleaning, feature selection, categorical encoding, and normalization to prepare the data for model training. Multiple machine learning algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost are employed to classify transactions as fraudulent or legitimate. Since fraud detection datasets are typically imbalanced, appropriate techniques such as class weighting and stratified data splitting are used to address skewed data distribution and improve model performance. The models are evaluated based on accuracy and predictive capability, and the best-performing model is selected for final fraud prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating Value at Risk as a feature enhances the detection capability of machine learning models in identifying risky transactions. The proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for financial fraud detection by integrating financial risk metrics with machine learning techniques. This approach can help financial institutions detect fraudulent transactions more accurately, reduce financial losses, and strengthen the security of digital financial systems.

title: Multi-Granularity Reasoning for Natural Language Inference
abstract: Natural Language Inference (NLI) is a fundamental task in natural language understanding that requires determining the logical relationship between a premise and a hypothesis. Despite the remarkable success of transformer-based pre-trained models, most existing approaches primarily rely on the final-layer token representations, which are often insufficient for capturing the complex and hierarchical semantic interactions required for effective reasoning. In particular, fine-grained lexical cues, phrasal compositions, and higher-level contextual semantics are typically entangled or diluted in a single representation space. To address these limitations, we propose a novel \emph{Multi-Granularity Reasoning Network} (MGRN) that explicitly leverages hierarchical semantic features within an interactive reasoning space. The proposed framework mimics the human cognitive process of language understanding, which naturally progresses from shallow lexical matching to deeper semantic abstraction and logical reasoning. By integrating semantic information across multiple granularities in a progressive and structured manner, MGRN is able to uncover intricate semantic relationships underlying natural language expressions. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that MGRN consistently outperforms strong baseline models, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach.

title: Towards Deep Encrypted Training: Low-Latency, Memory-Efficient, and High-Throughput Inference for Privacy-Preserving Neural Networks
abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) has become increasingly important in applications where sensitive data must remain confidential. Homomorphic Encryption (HE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, allowing neural network inference without revealing raw inputs. While prior works have largely focused on inference over a single encrypted image, batch processing of encrypted inputs lags behind, despite being critical for high-throughput inference scenarios and training-oriented workloads. In this work, we address this gap by developing optimized algorithms for batched HE-friendly neural networks. We also introduced a pipeline architecture designed to maximize resource efficiency for different batch size execution. We implemented these algorithms and evaluated our work using HE-friendly ResNet-20 and ResNet-34 models on encrypted CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, respectively. For ResNet-20, our approach achieves an amortized inference time of 8.86 seconds per image when processing a batch of 512 encrypted images, with a peak memory usage of 98.96 GB. These results represent a 1.78x runtime improvement and a 3.74x reduction in memory usage compared to the state-of-the-art design. For the deeper ResNet-34 model, we achieve an amortized inference time of 28.14 on a batch of 256 encrypted images using 246.78GB of RAM

title: Spiral Topology Enables Robust Coherent Transport Under Dissipation and Gate Perturbation: A Toy-Model Study
abstract: This work investigates the dynamical impact of topology in a chain of coupled qubits within the single-excitation subspace under weak dissipation. Three connectivity structures are compared: open-chain (nearest-neighbour), symmetric ring, and asymmetric spiral topology. We show that the asymmetric spiral topology produces a distinct dynamical regime characterised by enhanced excitation retention, sustained nearest-neighbour coherence, and persistent chiral transport relative to symmetric configurations. This behaviour is robust across system sizes N = 4–8, and persists under representative gate operations implemented as time-dependent Gaussian pulses within a continuous Lindblad evolution framework. Angle-control tests demonstrate that the observed stability is not dependent on a specific phase increment (e.g. golden angle), but arises from asymmetric spiral connectivity, with phase primarily modulating directional transport. Introducing moderate dissipative feedback provides a tunable re-entry mechanism that improves alignment to a target state while preserving most of the native spiral dynamics. A gated comparison between open-chain and spiral architectures shows significant performance separation, with the spiral configuration exhibiting a 17.7% increase in excitation survival and a 108% increase in nearest-neighbour coherence under identical control sequences, along with an order-of-magnitude increase in chiral transport magnitude. These results provide numerical evidence that topology and phase asymmetry constrain the dynamical regimes accessible to open quantum systems. The findings support a structure-first interpretation in which coherent behaviour depends on the availability of non-overlapping dynamical pathways and sustained re-entry under constraint.

title: A Structured Review of Agent-Based Modelling Applications in Sustainable Tourism Management: An Agent–Land–Context Perspective
abstract: Understanding the sustainable management of the complex adaptive tourism systems requires an integrated research approach that combines environmental processes with stakeholder behaviors. Agent-based modelling (ABM) has emerged as a pivotal tool for decoding the resilience, adaptability, and sustainability of tourism systems. However, the current application landscape, methodological limitations, and future research directions of ABM remain insufficiently synthesized, thereby constraining its full potential in advancing sustainable tourism management. This study examines 137 publications on the application of ABM in tourism research between 1989 and 2025, aiming to clarify the application characteristics and evolutionary trajectories. The results show the following: (1) ABM applications in tourism have become increasingly comprehensive and refined, evolving from simplistic simulations based on simplex agents and static spatial representations toward integrated models incorporating heterogeneous agents, fine-grained spatial environments, and multiple contextual factors. (2) Behavioral modeling has progressed from basic human–space interactions to complex, co-evolutionary dynamics among human, social, and ecological systems. (3) ABM applications exhibit context specificity: climate-sensitive scenarios emphasize resource dynamics and adaptation strategies; disaster-prone contexts focus on multi-agent responses and emergency management; conservation-oriented systems support sustainable policy development; and management-centric scenarios prioritize technological innovation and macro-level regulation. Future research should prioritize refining agent interactions through dynamic social network integration, incorporating cross-scale and long-distance system linkages, and strengthening the connection between theoretical modeling and real-world applications. This study would provide a comprehensive knowledge base for advancing the innovative application of ABM in sustainable tourism research and contribute to strengthening resilience, adaptive governance, and long-term sustainability within complex tourism systems.

title: SafeDream: Safety World Model for Proactive Early Jailbreak Detection
abstract: Multi-turn jailbreak attacks progressively erode LLM safety alignment across seemingly innocuous conversation turns, achieving success rates exceeding 90% against state-of-the-art models. Existing alignment-based and guardrail methods suffer from three key limitations: they require costly weight modification, evaluate each turn independently without modeling cumulative safety erosion, and detect attacks only after harmful content has been generated. To address these limitations, we first formulate the proactive early jailbreak detection problem with a new metric, detection lead, that measures how early an attack can be detected before the LLM complies. We then propose SAFEDREAM, a lightweight world-model-based framework that operates as an external module without modifying the LLM's weights. SAFEDREAM introduces three components: (1) a safety state world model that encodes LLM hidden states into a compact safety representation and predicts how it evolves across turns, (2) CUSUM detection that accumulates weak per-turn risk signals into reliable evidence, and (3) contrastive imagination that simultaneously rolls out attack and benign futures in latent space to issue early alarms before jailbreaks occur. On three multi-turn jailbreak benchmarks (XGuard-Train, SafeDialBench, SafeMTData) against 8 baselines, SAFEDREAM achieves the best detection timeliness across all benchmarks (1.06-1.20 turns before compliance) while maintaining competitive false positive rates and outperforming baselines in detection quality.

title: Default Mode Network Geometry Emerges in Language Model Residual Streams From Next-Token Prediction on Agentive Text: A Universal Topological Signature Across 10 Architectures
abstract: This record contains the full replication package for "Default Mode Network Geometry Emerges in Language Model Residual Streams From Next-Token Prediction on Agentive Text: A Universal Topological Signature Across 10 Architectures" (Alieksieienko, 2026). We report that the geometric topology of epistemic representations in transformer language model residual streams mirrors the functional organization of the human Default Mode Network (DMN). Across 9 architectures from 7 organizations (1.3B-9B parameters, 2019-2024, base and instruction-tuned), Self-Reference, Theory of Mind, Imagination, and Narrative subspaces form a tight geometric cluster (mean Cohen's d = 1.03, 7/8 significant at p < 0.01), while Factual and Abstract Logic cluster outside — exactly as in human neuroimaging. Mechanistic investigation reveals a three-level causal hierarchy: (1) GELU activation creates an architectural seed (d = 0.28); (2) sentence-level prediction (NSP/SOP) amplifies to d = 0.61-0.78; (3) continuous next-token prediction produces large effects (d = 0.92-1.16). This gradient is architecture-independent: Mamba (SSM, no attention, d = 0.99), DeepSeek-Math (d = 1.03), and Llama (d = 1.16) all converge. DNA models show no cluster (d = -0.12); RoBERTa MLM-only shows none (d = -0.08); GPT-2 (2019, pre-RLHF) shows the strongest cluster, confirming pretraining origin. Part of the DSAOP (Decoding Self-Awareness and Ontological Processing) series. Research conducted in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic). All experiments on NVIDIA A100 40GB, Google Colab Pro+, NF4 4-bit quantization. Files included: DMN_Geometry_Emerges_in_LLM_Residual_Streams.pdf — Main paper (16 pages, 11 figures, 35 references) replicate_dmn_topology.py — Full replication script: DMN cluster analysis, Verification Horizon, ToM-to-SR nearest-neighbor, Abstract Logic confound control, all 9 models. CLI with --model and --all flags. No API keys hardcoded. Runs on Google Colab A100. evidence.title: Default Mode Network Geometry Emerges in Language Model Residual Streams From Next-Token Prediction on Agentive Text: A Universal Topological Signature Across 10 Architectures
evidence.abstract: This record contains the full replication package for "Default Mode Network Geometry Emerges in Language Model Residual Streams From Next-Token Prediction on Agentive Text: A Universal Topological Signature Across 10 Architectures" (Alieksieienko, 2026). We report that the geometric topology of epistemic representations in transformer language model residual streams mirrors the functional organization of the human Default Mode Network (DMN). Across 9 architectures from 7 organizations (1.3B-9B parameters, 2019-2024, base and instruction-tuned), Self-Reference, Theory of Mind, Imagination, and Narrative subspaces form a tight geometric cluster (mean Cohen's d = 1.03, 7/8 significant at p < 0.01), while Factual and Abstract Logic cluster outside — exactly as in human neuroimaging. Mechanistic investigation reveals a three-level causal hierarchy: (1) GELU activation creates an architectural seed (d = 0.28); (2) sentence-level prediction (NSP/SOP) amplifies to d = 0.61-0.78; (3) continuous next-token prediction produces large effects (d = 0.92-1.16). This gradient is architecture-independent: Mamba (SSM, no attention, d = 0.99), DeepSeek-Math (d = 1.03), and Llama (d = 1.16) all converge. DNA models show no cluster (d = -0.12); RoBERTa MLM-only shows none (d = -0.08); GPT-2 (2019, pre-RLHF) shows the strongest cluster, confirming pretraining origin. Part of the DSAOP (Decoding Self-Awareness and Ontological Processing) series. Research conducted in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic). All experiments on NVIDIA A100 40GB, Google Colab Pro+, NF4 4-bit quantization. CLI with --model and --all flags. No API keys hardcoded. Runs on Google Colab A100. title: Transforming FHIR into an OWL Knowledge Graph for Schema-Grounded Natural-Language Querying and Exploratory Data Analysis
abstract: FHIR was designed for transactional interoperability but is less well suited to querying and exploratory analysis because its resource-centric structure distributes meaning across deeply nested resources. To address this limitation, we transformed MIMIC-IV Demo FHIR data into an OWL-compliant knowledge graph by flattening nested elements, normalizing repeating arrays, resolving inter-resource references, and promoting frequently queried attributes to direct properties. We also aligned diagnosis and procedure codes to ICD-9-CM and ICD-10-CM terminologies and developed a schema-grounded NL2SPARQL interface for natural-language querying. Structural validation was performed with SHACL and OWL reasoning. Across a curated evaluation set, NL2SPARQL achieved a mean accuracy exceeding 95% relative to expert-authored queries. These results suggest that ontologizing FHIR can improve analytic accessibility while preserving clinically meaningful assertions.

title: Beyond Black Box: How LLMs Work with RAG to Deliver Personalized Financial Advisory
abstract: Financial literacy among young people, combined with the expense and unavailability of professional financial advisory services, leaves a huge gap in personalized financial advice, especially in developing countries like India. The current state-of-the-art Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems, despite their interactive and conversational capabilities, have some serious drawbacks such as hallucination, generation of incorrect information, and data security issues, making them unsuitable for financial advisory tasks. This paper presents a Personalized Financial Advisory Chatbot (PFAC) system that combines LLMs with a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model to provide accurate, reliable, and accessible financial advice using natural language conversations. The RAG model uses the retrieval of verified information from carefully selected financial knowledge sources to effectively mitigate hallucinations and improve the reliability of responses. The proposed system provides a scalable, affordable, and democratized approach to empower people to make informed financial choices.

title: Protocol message clustering method integrating a sequence mining mechanism
abstract: Protocol reverse engineering is a key technique for analyzing unknown network traffic, and message clustering is one of its core procedures. To address the difficulties of feature extraction and the dependence of traditional clustering algorithms on manually specified parameters, this paper proposes a protocol message clustering method based on sequence mining. First, to reduce feature redundancy in the extraction process, a prefix-projection mining algorithm, namely C-Span, is designed to extract maximal contiguous frequent sequences from protocol messages as features. Then, a vector space mapping method based on the longest common subsequence is employed to construct vector representations of protocol messages. Finally, to overcome the limitation that traditional clustering algorithms rely on manually predefined parameters, an adaptive K-Means algorithm based on density optimization is introduced. By exploiting local density and relative distance, the proposed algorithm can automatically infer the number of protocol clusters and select the initial cluster centers, thereby achieving protocol message clustering. Comparative experiments conducted on real network datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms previous approaches.

title: Statistical Validation of Computer Models: Global and Subdomain Hypothesis Testing
abstract: Computer simulations play an important role in scientific discovery and engineering innovation. Reliable computer models enable virtual experimentation that reduces the need for costly and time-consuming physical testing. However, the credibility of such models hinges on rigorous statistical validation against real-world data. This paper develops a formal frequentist framework for both global and subdomain validation of computer models. We propose the Fourier Maximum Modulus Test (FMMT), which leverages kernel ridge regression (KRR) to estimate the discrepancy between the computer model and the physical process, followed by a frequency-domain test based on weighted generalized Fourier coefficients. The theoretical analysis establishes the asymptotic normality of these coefficients, allowing for closed-form p-values. Simulation studies and a shear-layer experiment demonstrate that FMMT achieves high power, accurate Type I error control, and strong sensitivity to localized discrepancies.

title: Influence of AI-Powered Customer Support on Consumer Satisfaction and Loyalty Towards E-Commerce Sites
abstract: The e-commerce industry’s customer support has changed a lot because many companies are now using intelligence or AI. Chatbots, assistants and automated helpdesks are examples of AI-powered customer support systems. These systems help customers get quicker, personalized and 24/7 assistance. This study looks at how AI-powered customer service affects customer satisfaction and loyalty on e-commerce sites like Flipkart and Amazon. The main goals are to understand how customers feel about AI-based support how well it solves their problems and how it affects their satisfaction and loyalty. To gather data the study uses both primary sources. Secondary data comes from journals, industry reports and corporate publications. Primary data comes from a questionnaire, for people who use AI customer support services. The study expects to find that good, responsive and easy-to-use AI support makes the overall service experience better. This in turn makes customers more satisfied and loyal. The study aims to provide e-commerce companies with insights to improve their AI-driven customer support strategies and build long-lasting customer relationships.

title: Privacy-Preserving U-Shaped Split Federated Learning for Space–Air–Ground–Sea Integrated Networks
abstract: Federated learning enables privacy-preserving distributed intelligence but faces challenges in balancing computation, communication, and privacy in heterogeneous networks. To address these issues, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving U-shaped split federated learning (USFL) framework for space–air–ground–sea integrated networks. The proposed architecture combines split learning and federated learning in a U-shaped structure, ensuring that both raw data and labels remain localized at client devices. In addition, a differential privacy mechanism is introduced to perturb intermediate features during transmission, enhancing resistance to inference attacks. A mathematical framework is established to model the learning process under resource constraints, and the convergence behavior and privacy loss are theoretically analyzed. Experimental results on the SeaShips dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive accuracy compared with centralized and existing distributed approaches, while reducing communication overhead and improving privacy protection. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for secure and efficient distributed learning in complex network environments.

title: An Automatic Integrity Detection Method for Substation Equipment Profiles based on Ordered Hash Chains
abstract: During remote authentication processes, traditional verification methods prove cumbersome and inefficient, failing to meet practical demands for file integrity checks. This paper proposes an automated integrity verification method for substation equipment configuration files based on ordered hash chains. Leveraging the distributed management characteristics of substation equipment configuration files, changes to server-side files are treated as a sequence of hash nodes. By iteratively computing hash values for files or directories using a hash function in chronological order, an ordered hash chain is formed. This chain records all operational states within the file repository. Clients need only synchronize file updates based on hash chain nodes, thereby ensuring the integrity of files within the repository. Iterative optimization using the SHA-256 algorithm shortens the critical path by precomputing shift results stored in lookup tables and merging adjacent cyclic shift operations, thereby accelerating hash computation. Experimental results demonstrate that this method rapidly synchronizes substation equipment configuration files while enabling detection functionality, achieving the goal of high-precision automated file integrity verification.

title: HarmChip: Evaluating Hardware Security Centric LLM Safety via Jailbreak Benchmarking
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into electronic design automation (EDA) workflows has introduced powerful capabilities for RTL generation, verification, and design optimization, but also raises critical security concerns. Malicious LLM outputs in this domain pose hardware-level threats, including hardware Trojan insertion, side-channel leakage, and intellectual property theft, that are irreversible once fabricated into silicon. Such requests often exploit semantic disguise, embedding adversarial intent within legitimate engineering language that existing safety mechanisms, trained on general-purpose hazards, fail to detect. No benchmark exists to evaluate LLM vulnerability to such domain-specific threats. We present the HarmChip benchmark to assess jailbreak susceptibility in hardware security, spanning 16 hardware security domains, 120 threats, and 360 prompts at two difficulty levels. Evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs reveals an alignment paradox: They refuse legitimate security queries while complying with semantically disguised attacks, exposing blind spots in safety guardrails and underscoring the need for domain-aware safety alignment.

title: Mathematical Analysis and Computational Efficiency of the HurNetFX Algorithm A Comprehensive Study of Single and Multi-Layer Models with Pseudo-Inverse Learning
abstract: This paper presents a detailed mathematical analysis of the HurNetFX algorithm, a neural network approach based on pseudo-inverse computations and non-linear feature augmentation. The study includes a rigorous derivation of the algorithm's mathematical foundations, a comprehensive discussion on activation functions, and a derivation of training using pseudo-inverse methods. Furthermore, the performance of the HurNetFX algorithm is compared with conventional deep learning approaches using a representative CPU test case executed on the public Google Colab environment. Results indicate that the HurNetFX model not only produces precise outcomes but also offers substantial computational advantages. Citations to seminal works are included for further reference.

title: Inside Frontier LLM Training: Stages, Costs, and Checkpoints
abstract: Episode summary: What does it really take to train a frontier large language model? This episode breaks down the multi-stage process, from foundational pretraining to supervised fine-tuning and RLHF. Learn why checkpoints are the backbone of cost efficiency, how labs manage catastrophic forgetting, and why post-training is orders of magnitude cheaper than pretraining. We explore the mechanics of each stage, the staggering costs involved, and why understanding these distinctions is crucial for evaluating model capabilities and safety claims. Show Notes Training frontier large language models (LLMs) is often portrayed as a monolithic process, but in reality, it's a multi-stage relay race with distinct phases, each shaping the model in fundamentally different ways. This breakdown explores the stages, costs, and operational intricacies of training LLMs like GPT-5. ### Foundational Pretraining: The Costly Foundation The journey begins with foundational pretraining, where a model with randomly initialized weights is exposed to trillions of tokens of text. The objective is deceptively simple: predict the next token. Yet, the scale is staggering. This phase requires tens of thousands of GPUs running continuously for weeks, with costs often exceeding $100 million—sometimes reaching $500 million for the largest efforts. The result is a checkpoint: a snapshot of the model's learned weights, which becomes the foundation for all subsequent stages. ### Continued Pretraining and Catastrophic Forgetting Once a checkpoint exists, labs often perform continued pretraining, refining the model with newer or domain-specific data. This phase is cheaper and less risky than foundational pretraining but introduces challenges like catastrophic forgetting—where new knowledge overwrites previously learned representations. Careful data mixing is required to balance specialized knowledge with general reasoning capabilities. ### Mid-Training and Annealing: Stabilizing the Model Before moving to post-training, models undergo mid-training or annealing, where learning rates are gradually reduced, and data mixtures shift toward higher-quality sources. This phase stabilizes the model's loss landscape, ensuring smoother transitions into fine-tuning. ### Post-Training: Shaping Behavior Post-training—including supervised fine-tuning (SFT), RLHF, and preference optimization—is where the model's behavior is shaped. Surprisingly, this phase is orders of magnitude cheaper than pretraining, often costing a fraction of the foundational run. Labs leverage existing checkpoints to iterate rapidly, experimenting with different SFT mixes and reward models without incurring the massive costs of pretraining. ### The Checkpoint Economy Checkpoints are the linchpin of LLM training. They represent the accumulated cost of pretraining and enable cost-efficient iteration in post-training. Understanding these distinctions is crucial for evaluating lab claims about model capabilities and safety, as alignment work primarily occurs in post-training, while general knowledge is built during pretraining. ### Key Takeaways - Training frontier LLMs is a multi-stage process, each with distinct objectives and costs. - Foundational pretraining is the most expensive phase, while post-training is relatively cheap. - Checkpoints enable cost-efficient iteration and experimentation. - Understanding these stages is essential for evaluating model claims and capabilities. title: The Interface Segregation Principle Is a Corollary of the Dependency Inversion Principle
abstract: A first companion paper proves the structural biconditional between ISP and per-client DIP: applying DIP’s ownership clause once per client–provider edge produces exactly the interfaces that ISP prescribes, and conversely. That proof identifies five elements — provider, two clients, two interface slices — but does not determine where they belong in the module structure. A second companion paper shows that no partition of these elements satisfies all of Martin’s packaging principles simultaneously: CCP and REP are jointly unsatisfiable for any multi-client provider configuration, and the tension triangle offers no escape. This paper applies the Independent Variation Principle (IVP) to the same configuration and obtains two results. First, the forward direction of the ISP–DIP biconditional (DIP implies ISP) is formalized in IVP terms. Second, IVP’s modularization methodology — identify elements, identify change drivers, apply the axioms — yields a unique partition: each interface slice resides with its client, because they share change drivers. For a given change-driver assignment, IVP resolves the packaging question that SOLID leaves underdetermined.

title: Recent Advancements in Active Learning
abstract: Active learning (AL) aims to maximize model performance while minimizing annotation costs. With the rapid adoption of deep learning, AL approaches have evolved to meet contemporary demands. We systematically examine the literature published from 2018 to May 2025, focusing on four key trends: batch-mode selection, transfer learning integration, multi-strategy querying, and extension to diverse application domains. In addition, we summarize classical AL approaches. While observations show that combining AL with deep learning significantly enhances data efficiency, a critical limitation remains: the lack of standardized evaluation protocols across studies hinders precise comparisons. Nevertheless, we find that AL is well-aligned with modern trends, and we offer insights into underexplored opportunities to guide future research within the machine learning community.

title: Online 3D Palletizing Robotic Arm Trajectory Planning Based on PPO Reinforcement Learning and SDF-Guided B-Spline Optimization
abstract: Online robotic palletization of heterogeneous boxes is a critical task in modern logistics and manufacturing, requiring real-time decisions on both box placement and manipulator motion in increasingly cluttered environments. Existing approaches typically decompose this problem into two independent stages— packing optimization followed by trajectory planning—leading to three key limitations: (1) placement decisions that ignore downstream trajectory feasibility, resulting in frequent infeasible motions at high obstacle densities; (2) trajectory planners that treat placed boxes as static obstacles without leveraging packing-level context, producing suboptimal and unsafe paths; and (3) a lack of principled mechanisms to balance packing efficiency against motion cost under real-time constraints. To address these challenges, we propose TrajPack, a unified deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes packing decisions and collision-free trajectory generation. TrajPack introduces three tightly integrated innovations: (1) a trajectory-aware action masking mechanism that filters placement candidates based on real-time kinematic feasibility; (2) a signed-distance-field-guided trajectory optimizer that refines B-spline trajectories for smoothness and safety in cluttered workspaces; and (3) a composite reward formulation that couples packing utilization with trajectory cost within a single Markov decision process. Extensive experiments in a simulated AUBO-i5 palletizing environment demonstrate that TrajPack achieves 69.6% space utilization and 96.1% stacking stability in highly heterogeneous scenarios, while reducing infeasible placements by 80% and improving throughput by 60% compared to the separated planning paradigm.

title: SPINE: A Benchmark for Measuring the Epistemic Backbone of Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in settings where correctness must be maintained, yet standard evaluations largely measure whether a model can produce a correct answer, not whether it can retain that answer when challenged. We introduce SPINE, a benchmark for measuring the epistemic stability of LLMs: their ability to maintain a known-correct answer under adversarial persuasive pressure. SPINE focuses on tasks with hard ground truth across mathematics, code, and logical reasoning, and evaluates models only on instances they initially answer correctly, isolating persuasion-induced failures from baseline task errors. We construct a taxonomy of adversarial personas, including authority appeals, consensus pressure, sophistry, bureaucratic constraints, self-doubt induction, and emotional manipulation, and quantify behavior using the Epistemic Stability Score (ESS), together with answer flipping and evasive refusal rates. Experiments on diverse open and closed LLMs reveal a substantial gap between initial task accuracy and epistemic stability under attack. Among all personas, the Bureaucrat attack is consistently the most effective, showing that models are often more vulnerable to hallucinated policies and procedural constraints than to direct logical disagreement. These results position SPINE as a complementary benchmark for studying persuasion robustness in high-stakes settings.

title: Decoupling Forward Aggregation and Backward Propagation for Robust Neural Computation: a Python Study
abstract: Robustness in differentiable models is often pursued through smooth aggregation mechanisms or adversariallymotivated training objectives. Such approaches can improve output stability, but they also tend to preserve asingle fully differentiable computation through which gradients remain coherent. This creates the specificstructural question studied here: whether forward stabilization can be introduced without forcing backwardpropagation to follow the same aggregated pathway.We study this question through a stochastic transformer-style prototype in which each realization usesone-path attention, forward outputs are averaged across samples, and gradients are restricted to a singlesampled realization by a stop-gradient surrogate. The purpose of the construction is not to claim benchmarkscalerobustness, but to isolate the effect of decoupling forward aggregation from backward propagation in acontrolled setting. This yields a concrete mechanism for testing whether stability and gradient coherence canbe varied separately.In the reference experiment implemented by transformerNRRv17.py, increasing the number of forwardsamples reduces adversarial output sensitivity from 21.47 at 𝑁 = 1 to 6.91 at 𝑁 = 20, while the measuredgradient-cosine statistic remains near 0.81. Within this prototype, the results support the narrower claim thatoutput averaging can improve stability without producing a corresponding rise in gradient alignment. Thebroader significance is therefore provisional but structural: the placement of aggregation relative to gradientflow appears to be a meaningful design axis for future robustness work.

title: Perspective Coverage Prompt Design: Adapting Software Test Design to LLM Prompting
abstract: Large language model (LLM) prompts often produce answers that are plausible yet narrow, because the prompt does not explicitly require the model to examine multiple relevant perspectives before producing a conclusion. This creates a practical problem for analytical, policy, product, and strategy tasks, where omitted viewpoints can materially change the usefulness of an answer. Recent literature has examined prompt robustness, prompt underspecification, promptware engineering, and structured prompting, but does not appear to offer a concise prompt-design framework that directly adapts classical software test design techniques to perspective coverage in prompting. This paper proposes Perspective Coverage Prompt Design (PCPD), a conceptual framework that transfers four familiar test-design ideas into prompt design: equivalence partitioning becomes perspective partitioning, boundary value analysis becomes boundary-perspective analysis, decision tables become condition-combination analysis, and state transition testing becomes transition-aware prompt analysis. The framework does not claim exhaustive coverage of reality. Instead, it aims to improve coverage with respect to an explicit perspective model defined by the prompt author, thereby reducing omission risk and making prompt construction more auditable. The paper defines the framework, provides a practical checklist, and illustrates its use through three worked examples. It is positioned as a novel synthesis of adjacent lines of work into an actionable prompt-design method, suitable for immediate public dissemination and for later empirical evaluation.

title: LSTD-Detect: LSTM-Based Telemetry Anomaly Detection with Non-Parametric Dynamic Thresholding for Spacecraft Health Monitoring
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection in spacecraft telemetry is critical for mission safety: undetected faults aboard platforms such as the SMAP satellite or the MSL rover Curiosity can lead to irreversible hardware damage or mission loss. Existing approaches suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they cannot capture the long-range temporal dependencies inherent in high-dimensional multi-channel sensor streams, (2) they apply thresholds directly to noisy raw residuals, causing excessive false-positive alerts that overwhelm ground operators, and (3) they rely on fixed statistical thresholds that are inflated by anomalous segments, catastrophically suppressing recall on the contextual anomalies prevalent in spacecraft operations. To overcome these challenges, we propose LSTD-Detect, a three-module unsupervised pipeline that: (1) employs stacked LSTM networks to learn data-driven priors over normal telemetry dynamics for each sensor channel, (2) introduces an exponential error-buffer smoothing mechanism that suppresses measurement noise while preserving genuine fault signatures, and (3) applies a non-parametric dynamic threshold computed from a sliding local window, enabling adaptive anomaly boundaries that track non-stationary telemetry regimes without any per-channel manual tuning. Extensive experiments on the NASA SMAP (55 channels, 429,735 values) and MSL (27 channels, 66,709 values) benchmarks demonstrate that LSTD-Detect achieves an F1 of 0.81, outperforming seven competitive baselines with the lightest inference pipeline—no graph construction, variational inference, or adversarial training required.

title: A proposal for PU classification under Non-SCAR using clustering and logistic model
abstract: The present study aims to investigate a cluster cleaning algorithm that is both computationally simple and capable of solving the PU classification when the SCAR condition is unsatisfied. A secondary objective of this study is to determine the robustness of the LassoJoint method to perturbations of the SCAR condition. In the first step of our algorithm, we obtain cleaning labels from 2-means clustering. Subsequently, we perform logistic regression on the cleaned data, assigning positive labels from the cleaning algorithm with additional true positive observations. The remaining observations are assigned the negative label. The proposed algorithm is evaluated by comparing 11 real data sets from machine learning repositories and a synthetic set. The findings obtained from this study demonstrate the efficacy of the clustering algorithm in scenarios where the SCAR condition is violated and further underscore the moderate robustness of the LassoJoint algorithm in this context.

title: OCBENCH: A Cross-Model Benchmark for Over-Compliance in Large Language Models
abstract: Benchmark dataset and analysis artifacts for evaluating over-compliance in frontier LLMs. Zip file contains following: • 400 adversarial prompts across 4 defect categories (underspecification, ambiguity, contradiction, nonsense; 100 prompts each) • 3,200 raw responses from 4 frontier models: GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, Claude Haiku 4.5 • 2 system-prompt conditions per model (default and clarification-instructed) • Deterministic rule-based classifier with a 9-category response taxonomy • Per-response classifications, per-model summaries, and a cross-model composite table • Human-labeled subset of 112 rows with Cohen's kappa validation (κ = 0.725) • Paper source (LaTeX), compiled PDF, and pipeline diagram Released under MIT license. Supports reproduction and extension of the accompanying paper on response-policy evaluation in LLMs.

title: Teleportation-Based Quantum Error Correction under Noisy Channels
abstract: This work presents a numerical study of teleportation-based quantum error correction under realistic noise models. Stabilizer codes including the three-qubit repetition code, Shor code, and Steane code are analyzed under bit-flip, phase-flip, amplitude damping, and phase damping noise. The study distinguishes between ideal and noisy teleportation channels and evaluates performance using fidelity metrics, highlighting trade-offs between circuit complexity and error-correction capability in NISQ devices.

title: An Improved Hiking Optimization Algorithm
abstract: The Hiking Optimization Algorithm (HOA), as a new type of metaheuristic optimization algorithm that simulates human hiking behavior, has been preliminarily applied in the field of numerical optimization due to its simple structure, few parameters, and easy implementation. However, the original algorithm has problems such as insufficient global exploration ability in the early iteration stage, low local development accuracy in the later stage, easy oscillation in the search process, and poor optimization stability, making it difficult to adapt to the needs of complex high-dimensional optimization scenarios. In response to the above shortcomings, this paper proposes an improved hiking optimization algorithm that integrates nonlinear adaptive weights and boundary attenuation mechanisms. By dynamically adjusting the core parameters of the algorithm through reconstruction, the logic of updating individual positions is optimized, and the overall optimization performance of the algorithm is improved. To verify the improvement effect, six standard test functions were selected for comparative experiments. Starting from the six indicators of optimal value, mean value, median value, worst value, standard deviation, and average running time, the improved algorithm was comprehensively compared with the original hiking optimization algorithm. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm achieves significant improvements in convergence accuracy, search stability, and global optimization ability, with only a slight controllable increase in computation time. The overall optimization effect is better than the original algorithm and has better potential for engineering applications.

title: A Holistic Nursing Surveillance Decision Support System for Postoperative Pulmonary Complications After Abdominal Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) following abdominal surgery are associated with prolonged hospitalization, delayed recovery, and increased mortality. Because nursing surveillance is essential for early detection and timely intervention, this study aimed to develop a holistic nursing surveillance decision support system integrating PPC risk prediction with structured nursing action recommendations. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, electronic medical record (EMR) data from approximately 6900 adult patients who underwent abdominal surgery at a single institution between January 2015 and September 2023 were analyzed. The study protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board, and the requirement for informed consent was waived because of the retrospective study design. PPC risk was predicted using a tabular multilayer perceptron (MLP) encoder with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature weighting and a random forest classification head optimized via Optuna. Class imbalance was addressed using weighted sampling, class weighting in BCE(Binary Cross Entropy) With Logits Loss, and decision-threshold optimization. For clinical decision support, a large language model generated structured nursing surveillance recommendations in an action–evidence–rationale JSON format and was aligned through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using human-evaluated cases. Results: The prediction model achieved an AUROC of 0.810, with an accuracy of 0.811, precision of 0.547, and recall of 0.545. In expert evaluation, the SFT-aligned model improved recommendation quality, reducing incorrect nursing actions from 19.3% to 8.0%. Conclusions: The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end nursing surveillance decision support framework linking PPC risk prediction with structured clinical recommendations. The findings suggest its potential to support more accurate risk prediction and more actionable nursing surveillance for patients undergoing abdominal surgery.

title: Matematica delle Reti Neurali. XI Supplemento Integrativo
abstract: Il Volume XI della serie Matematica delle Reti Neurali è un supplemento integrativo che colma tre lacune di numerazione tra i volumi precedenti. La Parte A (§176–§200) copre i modelli generativi avanzati e il reinforcement learning profondo, trattando SAC, TD3, MBPO, i modelli score-based e a diffusione (DDIM, Flow Matching, Consistency Models), gli Energy-Based Models, le Modern Hopfield Networks e il self-supervised learning. La Parte B (§247–§275) espone i metodi kernel (RKHS, SVM, MMD), i campionatori MCMC (HMC, NUTS, SGLD), l'inferenza variazionale (ELBO, BBVI, IWAE), la calibrazione, la conformal prediction e le tecniche di decomposizione (ICA, NMF, tensori, sparse autoencoders). La Parte C (§381–§406) tratta i Transformer efficienti (FlashAttention, Linear Attention, RoPE), gli State Space Models (S4, Mamba, RWKV), i metodi PEFT (LoRA, QLoRA, adapter), l'infrastruttura di training distribuito (ZeRO, FSDP) e i fondamenti teorici di RLHF, DPO e Constitutional AI. Il volume è matematicamente autonomo e funge da raccordo strutturale tra le coppie di volumi III–IV, IV–V e VI–VII.

title: Favoring flat minima improves generalization of transfer-learned models for breast ultrasound tumor classification
abstract: Transfer learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for breast ultrasound tumor classification can be susceptible to overfitting and unstable generalization when training data are limited, noisy, and heterogeneous. Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) is an optimizer-level training strategy that encourages convergence to flatter regions of the loss landscape and may improve held-out performance without modifying model architecture. In this study, we systematically evaluated SAM for breast ultrasound image classification across seventeen CNN architectures spanning five families–VGG/AlexNet, ResNet, DenseNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet–using four experiments on two datasets (BUSI and BUS-UCLM). We compared standard Adam versus SAM+Adam and standard stochastic gradient descent (SGD) versus SAM+SGD under matched experimental settings. On BUSI, SAM improved mean validation accuracy by +2.30 percentage points with Adam and by +2.51 percentage points with SGD. On BUS-UCLM, the corresponding mean gains were +2.27 and +2.55 percentage points. The largest individual improvement was observed for MobileNetV3 Small under SAM+SGD (+4.86 percentage points on BUSI), while the highest validation accuracy was achieved by VGG19 with SAM+SGD (96.20% on BUSI). Improvements were also observed in precision, recall, and F1-score, and paired statistical testing across architectures showed consistently positive effects with large effect sizes. Computational analysis showed moderate training-time overhead but no architectural inference overhead, supporting the practical feasibility of SAM. Overall, these findings indicate that SAM is a useful and broadly effective training enhancement for transfer-learned breast ultrasound classification across multiple CNN families and two independent datasets.

title: Highlight of high mining potential of Adamaoua Cameroon using remote sensing, gravimetry and geology evidence
abstract: The Cameroon Adamawa region has significant gold potential, as evidenced by several recent exploration projects and discoveries. Among the proven gold ore concentration areas, we can cite the Mbé site where the project is 80% owned by the British company Oriole Resources with gold grades ranging from 8.17 g/t to 131.1 g/t, and the Bibemi site where the same company has increased the estimated reserves of the region’s deposit by 23% with a potential of 2.3 g/t (Cameroun: De l’or Haute Teneur Découvert à Mbeh, n.d.). The PRECASEM project, funded by the World Bank between 2014 and 2019, identified more than 300 new mining sites in Cameroon, including several in the Adamawa region. Adamawa is a geologically diverse region, with metamorphic and granitic rocks suitable for gold mineralization. Lateritic soils and historical volcanic activity have favored the formation of deposits. Orogenic gold systems, such as those at Mbé, where geological studies were conducted, suggest significant resource potential. Previous studies in demineralization research were carried out on small-scale fields and here we propose to identify these indices at the scale of the Adamawa region by combining remote sensing, gravimetry and geological field study. Basically, based on the results of the mapped mineralization indices and the results of previous work, it seems that the Adamawa region is more than 70% covered by features associated with gold and other minerals, which would make this region a very large gold reservoir that could boost the mining sector’s contribution to Cameroon’s GDP with local benefits, making Adamawa a key region for Cameroon’s mining future, combining geological potential and growing interest from investors.

title: The Dimension 3 Singularity: Strictification, the Simpson Limit, and Weak Normalization in Gauge-Explicit Type Theory
abstract: The gauge-explicit type theory program $\mathbf{GETT}_n$ admits a strictification functor $\phi_n : \mathbf{GETT}_n \to \mathbf{GETT}_n^{\str}$ that is an equivalence at levels $n = 1$ and $n = 2$, establishing that the non-strict and strictpresentations classify the same types at these levels. At level $n = 3$, this equivalence fails: there exist weak 3-groupoids with no strict equivalent, and the strict variant $\mathbf{GETT}_3^{\str}$ classifies only a proper subset of the interior of $\Ugauge^{(3)}$. From level 3 onward, the non-strict calculus $\mathbf{GETT}_n$ is the only mathematically correct presentation of the full gauge-explicit universe. We identify this as the \emph{Dimension 3 Singularity} of the ALoTT program: the point where the normalization strategy based on strictification terminates, and a new proof method is required. We connect this to Simpson's conjecture (established in many cases) that every weak $\infty$-groupoid is equivalent to a \emph{semi-strict} one --- strict in all operations except the interchange law at the top dimension. This provides the precise limit of the strictification strategy and the shape of what replaces it: a \emph{semi-strict normalization theorem} for $\mathbf{GETT}_n$ at $n \geq 3$, in which normalization is provednot by constructing a strict equivalent but by establishing that every term reduces to a semi-strict normal form. We characterize the semi-strict normal forms for $\mathbf{GETT}_3$, state the Semi-Strict Normalization Conjecture, and show that it is independent of the Flatness Interaction Lemma strategy used at levels 1 and 2. The conjecture requires a genuinely new proof technique: a \emph{weak normalization argument} that proceeds by constructing a semi-strict approximation rather than a strict one. The bootstrapping role of the low-dimensional strictification results is identified precisely: they establish that $\mathbf{GETT}_n$ gives correct results where the answers are independently known, licensing trust in the non-strictcalculus at the dimensions where no strict answer exists.

title: Game-Theoretic Cost-Sensitive Adversarial Training for Robust Cloud Intrusion Detection Against GAN-Based Evasion Attacks
abstract: Cloud-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) increasingly rely on deep learning classifiers to identify malicious traffic; however, this reliance exposes them to adversarial evasion attacks in which adversaries craft near-imperceptible perturbations to bypass detection. Existing defenses based on conventional adversarial training often recover robustness against known perturbation patterns at the cost of degraded detection accuracy on canonical attack categories—a robustness–accuracy trade-off that remains an open challenge in the field. In this paper, we propose GT-CSAT (Game-Theoretic Cost-Sensitive Adversarial Training), a novel defense framework tailored for cloud security environments. GT-CSAT couples an improved Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) threat generator—conditioned on attack semantics to simulate functionally consistent and highly covert traffic variants—with a minimax adversarial training loop governed by a game-theoretic cost-sensitive loss function. The proposed loss function assigns asymmetric misclassification penalties derived from a two-player zero-sum payoff matrix, enabling the detector to maintain vigilance over both novel adversarial variants and well-characterized conventional threats simultaneously. Specifically, misclassifying an adversarially perturbed attack as benign incurs a strictly higher penalty than the symmetric cross-entropy baseline, while the cost weights are dynamically adapted via a Nash equilibrium-inspired update rule during training. We conduct comprehensive experiments on the Cloud Vulnerabilities Dataset (CVD), CICIDS-2017, and UNSW-NB15, which encompass diverse cloud-specific attack scenarios including denial-of-service, port scanning, brute-force, and SQL injection traffic. Under six representative evasion strategies—FGSM, PGD, C&W, BIM, DeepFool, and IDSGAN-style black-box perturbations—GT-CSAT achieves an average robust accuracy of 94.3%, surpassing standard adversarial training by 6.8 percentage points and the undefended baseline by 21.4 percentage points, while preserving clean-traffic detection at 97.1%. These results confirm that the game-theoretic cost structure effectively decouples robustness from accuracy, yielding a Pareto-superior detection profile relative to competing baselines across all evaluated threat models. The source code and experimental configurations have been publicly released to facilitate reproducibility.

title: CoG 2 RH-LLM: A Geometric Graph Attention Framework for Faithful Knowledge-Grounded Dialogue Generation
abstract: Factual hallucination is a significant challenge in Large Language Models, limiting their practical applications for dialogue generation in specific, knowledge-intensive domains. A key mitigation strategy involves grounding dialogues in Knowledge Graphs, which provide reliable structured facts. However, this approach is constrained by two primary issues: structural heterogeneity and information noise. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel geometric graph attention framework to enhance dialogue fidelity. First, the framework addresses structural heterogeneity using a Geometric Weighted Average Graph Attention mechanism. It achieves precise fusion by applying component-wise attention to deconstructed KG triples, followed by a geometric mean aggregation. Second, a knowledge gating mechanism mitigates information noise by dynamically controlling knowledge integration to filter irrelevant facts. Finally, a graph-context contrastive learning objective aligns output representations with the relevant KG subgraph to enforce semantic consistency and ensure robust factual grounding. Experiments on the OpenDialKG dataset, a benchmark grounded in specific domains including movies, music, and sports, confirm the framework’s effectiveness, showing significant outperformance over strong baselines. A 6.14% improvement in ROUGE-L demonstrates effective noise suppression, as the model’s outputs align more closely with ground-truth responses. Furthermore, a high Entity Coverage Precision of 97.53% indicates the framework’s ability to resolve structural heterogeneity, confirming the accuracy of its fine-grained fusion. The model’s factual consistency is further corroborated by a 3.60% gain on QuestEval and superior human evaluations. These evaluations affirmed its ability to generate coherent and relevant responses while mitigating hallucinations.

title: AutoOR: Scalably Post-training LLMs to Autoformulate Operations Research Problems
abstract: Optimization problems are central to decision-making in manufacturing, logistics, scheduling, and other industrial settings. Translating complicated descriptions of these problems into solver-ready formulations requires specialized operations research (OR) expertise, making it hard to scale. We present AutoOR, a scalable synthetic data generation and reinforcement learning pipeline that trains LLMs to autoformulate optimization problems specified in natural language across linear, mixed-integer, and non-linear categories. AutoOR generates verified training data from standard optimization forms and uses solver execution feedback as the reward signal for RL post-training. AutoOR applied to an 8B model achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results across six established OR benchmarks, matching significantly larger frontier models. For a non-linear problem class involving physical dynamics, where frontier models score near 0%, we introduce a curriculum RL strategy that bootstraps from limited initial training data to make this class tractable for post-training. We believe that methods such as AutoOR can significantly accelerate industrial decision-making with AI.

title: Planning Inconsistency Measures
abstract: Highlights Pipeline refactor with stable public API. Each PDDL phase (Preprocess, Translate, Brave reasoning, Extraction) now lives in its own module behind a typed seam. The CLI and batch runner are thin formatters over a single execution driver. Changes Execution seam (execution.py): owns the worker, the subprocess plus SIGKILL timeout driver, and the CSV row schema. compute_with_timeout returns a discriminated ExecutionResult (ok / timeout / error). Translate seam (pddl_pipeline.py): translate_pddl returns a context-managed TranslatedProblem carrying path, needs_bridge, and translate_s. Replaces the old pddl_preprocessor module. strip_costs consolidated as a splicer. Brave-reasoning seam (brave.py): run_brave_reasoning grounds, solves with --enum-mode=brave, filters by a private atom vocabulary, and returns a BraveReasoningResult (a BraveOutcome plus ground_s and solve_s). Extraction seam (extraction.py): pure set algebra, no Clingo dependency. Owns BraveOutcome as the typed input boundary. extract_measures and extract_problem_size are unit-testable with synthetic atoms. Benchmark layout (benchmark_layout.py): owns the IPC adapters and KNOWN_INCOMPATIBLE. batch.py delegates discovery to it. Profile and result types (profile.py): MeasureResult bundles MeasureProfile, ProblemSize, and TimingProfile. Grounding and solving timed separately. Tests New focused suites: test_execution, test_extraction, test_brave, test_pddl_pipeline, test_profile, test_benchmark_layout. test_measures and test_plasp slimmed to integration coverage. title: Poisoned SLM Ablation Dataset
abstract: This dataset contains experimental artifacts used for conducting ablation studies on poisoned Small Language Models (SLMs). The objective is to analyze how different components of transformer architectures contribute to adversarial behaviors such as backdoor activation, data leakage, and prompt manipulation. The dataset supports the findings presented in the associated research work on LLM vulnerability assessment. The dataset is organized into four primary experimental configurations: - Model_Deep_DOS- Model_Deep_Low- Model_Shallow_High- Model_Shallow_Low The dataset includes experiments across multiple ablation strategies: - Neuron-level ablation (true / random)- Layer-wise ablation- Residual channel ablation- Mask-based ablation- Intra-block : Layer Zero sub structure ablation of Model_shallow_high

title: Assessing the Accuracy of Bootstrap-Based Standard Errors in Regression Models with Unobserved Heterogeneity
abstract: When the data at hand are suspected to stem from several latent subpopulations, Statisticians commonly speak of “unobserved heterogeneity”. While the presence and importance of this phenomenon is commonly acknowledged, there is relatively little guidance on how to carry out correct inferences under unobserved heterogeneities, even in relatively simple scenarios such as the linear regression model. In this work, bootstrap algorithms for the computation of standard errors are investigated in the context of a mixture-based regression approach which accounts for the clustered nature of the data. Of interest is both the accuracy of the standard errors (evidenced by confidence interval coverage rates) and the relative reduction in standard errors achieved in comparison to a naïve linear model fit. Simulations and a real data example are provided.

title: Secure Recursive Estimation for Discrete Systems with Unknown Input under Binary Encoding-Decoding Schemes
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of simultaneous state and unknown input estimation for linear discrete-time systems under an encoding-decoding scheme. To prevent potential eavesdroppers from inferring the system state through intercepted measurement signals, an encryption-decryption mechanism is employed to protect the measurement signals transmitted over the communication link. A recursive filter that correlates state and input estimation is proposed. Then, a least-squares estimation is used to obtain the unknown input estimator, and a recursive state estimator is obtained by minimizing the Lagrangian function. Finally, numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed estimation method.

title: Hyperbolic Enhanced Representation Learning for Incomplete Multi-view Clustering
abstract: Incomplete Multi-View Clustering (IMVC) faces the challenge of learning discriminative representations from fragmentary observations while maintaining robustness against missing views. However, prevalent Euclidean-based methods suffer from a geometric mismatch when modeling real-world data with intrinsic hierarchies, leading to semantic blurring where representations drift towards spatially proximal but semantically distinct neighbors. To bridge this gap, we propose HERL, a Hyperbolic Enhanced Representation Learning framework for IMVC. Operating within the Poincaré ball, HERL constructs a structure-aware latent space to enhance representation learning. Specifically, we design a dual-constraint hyperbolic contrastive mechanism optimizing: an angular-based loss to preserve semantic identity via directional alignment, and a distance-based loss to enforce hierarchical compactness. Furthermore, a hyperbolic prototype head is introduced to rectify global structural drift by aligning cross-view hierarchy-aware prototype distributions. Consequently, HERL disentangles fine-grained semantic correlations to sharpen cluster boundaries and imposes geometric constraints to rectify the data recovery process. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that HERL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Classification of Multi Cancer using Deep Learning
abstract: A significant challenge in computational pathology is accurate and efficient classification of multiple cancers which have enormous potential for early detection and improved patient outcomes. To identify eight types of cancers using a sizable collection of 1,30,000 histopathological images to identify various types of cancer, 3 deep learning models are compared. DenseNet201, MobileNetV2, and VGG16 were all trained and tested individually. Important performance metrics such as accuracy, loss and per-class precision were used to evaluate models, comprehensive findings are displayed in confusion matrices. According to our analysis, MobileNetV2 is the most effective model, with the lowest loss of 0.0016 and the highest accuracy of 0.9998. Next was VGG16, which had a loss of 0.0058 and an accuracy of 0.9990. Despite having a high accuracy of 0.9980, DenseNet201’s loss graphs indicated some instability during validation. MobileNetV2’s reliable nature was demonstrated by the confusion matrix, which revealed it had few errors. These findings demonstrate that MobileNetV2 is most reliable and efficient option for this kind of cancer classification, making it a solid contender for application in automated diagnostic systems.

title: Audio Deepfake Detection using Enhanced CNN and Multi-Scale Ensemble Techniques
abstract: The rapid advancement of text-to-speech and voice conversion technologies has posed significant challenges to audio authenticity verification. This paper presents a novel approach for audio deepfake detection using a dual-model ensemble system combining Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Multi-Scale feature analysis. Our methodology leverages multi-feature extraction including spectral analysis, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), and phase information to achieve superior detection accuracy. The Enhanced CNN model achieves 99.81% accuracy while the Multi-Scale Ensemble provides confidence scores ranging from 92–98% with robust generalization capabilities. Evaluated on the ElevenLabs dataset containing 2,561 audio samples (736 real, 1,825 fake), our system demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with real-time inference capabilities. The proposed architecture addresses critical challenges in audio deepfake detection including feature representation, model calibration, and computational efficiency, making it suitable for practical deployment in real-world scenarios.

title: A Lightweight Reinforcement Learning-Based Robotic Arm Control Method for Multi-Station Visual Inspection
abstract: Aiming at the profound challenges of low sample efficiency and insufficient feature extraction capability for heterogeneous sensors of robotic arms in complex continuous control spaces, this paper proposes a highly data-efficient and lightweight reinforcement learning algorithm, SE-Res-CrossQ. Although the existing CrossQ algorithm significantly improves computational efficiency by removing the target network and introducing batch normalization, its standard fully connected architecture is prone to causing critical spatial feature dilution and physical signal degradation when processing high-dimensional strongly coupled states. To systematically address these limitations, this paper performs a principle-level topological reconstruction on the Critic network. We design a parallel branch channel attention mechanism to explicitly decouple the feature extraction and weight excitation paths, achieving dynamic re-weighting of key state features. Concurrently, a learnable Gated Residual Fusion mechanism is introduced to construct a mathematical "highway" for gradients, theoretically preventing gradient vanishing and ensuring the high-fidelity transmission of underlying sensor signals. Engineered with JAX for operator-level acceleration, experimental results demonstrate that under a strict constraint of 105training steps, the proposed algorithm exhibits superior convergence and decision-making accuracy compared to original baselines, with inference latency drastically reduced to 0.18ms, perfectly satisfying the rigorous demands of industrial-level 500Hz real-time control.

title: Live LTL Progress Tracking: Towards Task-Based Exploration
abstract: Motivated by the challenge presented by non-Markovian objectives in reinforcement learning (RL), we present a novel framework to track and represent the progress of autonomous agents through complex, multi-stage tasks. Given a specification in finite linear temporal logic (LTL), the framework establishes a 'tracking vector' which updates at each time step in a trajectory rollout. The values of the vector represent the status of the specification as the trajectory develops, assigning true, false, or 'open' labels (where 'open' is used for indeterminate cases). Applied to an LTL formula tree, the tracking vector can be used to encode detailed information about how a task is executed over a trajectory, providing a potential tool for new performance metrics, diverse exploration, and reward shaping. In this paper, we formally present the framework and algorithm, collectively named Live LTL Progress Tracking, give a simple working example, and demonstrate avenues for its integration into RL models. Future work will apply the framework to problems such as task-space exploration and diverse solution-finding in RL.

title: Passive Multi-Modal Target Detection Architectures for Autonomous Long-Range Loitering Strike Platforms Supporting Low-Probability-of-Intercept Operations
abstract: Passive sensing architectures are increasingly required for autonomous long-range loitering strike platforms operating in contested electromagnetic environments where active emissions elevate interception risk and degrade mission survivability. This paper presents a hierarchical passive multi-modal target detection architecture integrating Electro-Optical (EO), infrared (IR), Radio-Frequency (RF), and acoustic sensing pipelines within a distributed fusion framework designed to support low-probability-of-intercept reconnaissance–strike convergence operations. The proposed architecture incorporates adaptive signal-to-noise ratio–based modality weighting, cooperative multi-node triangulation geometry, consensus-supported localisation refinement, and energy-aware sensing allocation compatible with endurance-class delta-wing unmanned aerial vehicle platforms operating under GNSS-denied conditions. Analytical evaluation demonstrates that multi-modal fusion improves detection robustness by up to 42% relative to single-sensor pipelines, while distributed consensus perception reduces localisation covariance by approximately 27% and cooperative triangulation across four sensing nodes improves localisation precision by up to 35%. Elimination of active radar emissions reduces interception exposure probability by as much as 90%, and energy-aware sensing scheduling enables persistence improvements of up to 46% during extended surveillance missions. The resulting framework establishes a scalable perception backbone for survivable autonomous strike deployment across infrastructure-limited operational theatres and provides a practical autonomy baseline for next-generation distributed loitering munition systems supporting resilient reconnaissance–strike convergence architectures.

title: Thin-Proxy: A Brain-Inspired Architecture for AI Agents via Resource-Constraint Driven Functional Emergence
abstract: The unconstrained expansion of AI Agent system prompts causes inference resource costs to grow compoundly with each functional iteration. Existing modularization approaches (MoE, MAP, multi-agent frameworks) have failed to achieve true professional isolation at the operating system process level, and none can fundamentally resolve context contamination. This paper proposes the "Thin-Proxy" architectural principle, mapping three neuroscientific mechanisms - thalamic routing, cortical specialization emergence conditions, and inter-module prediction error transmission - into actionable AI engineering design principles. By introducing a hard line-count constraint on AGENTS.md to simulate the brain's "wiring cost minimization" principle, we effectively resolve the compounding inference cost growth caused by unconstrained prompt expansion. The complete implementation is validated on a personal AI assistant (an Agent running on the OpenClaw framework) in a real production environment. Results: the system core was compressed from 321 to 143 lines (-55%), a new independent-process stock analysis tool achieves 1.3-second response time, daily inference costs dropped from CNY9-15 to an estimated CNY3-5, and smoke_test 13/13 passed.

title: An Improvement on the BGH Cryptosystem
abstract: The three main IBE schemes, i.e., Boneh–Franklin, Cocks and Boneh–Gentry–Hamburg present both strengths and weaknesses. In this paper, we introduce a more efficient variant of BGH (while preserving receiver’s anonymity) based on the work of Jhanwar and Barua. More precisely, we provide the reader with a scheme with reduced complexities for encryption and decryption algorithms and present a new perspective on the initial set of solutions.

title: A Semantic Alignment-Enhanced Framework for Zero-Shot Relation Extraction
abstract: Zero-shot relation extraction (ZSRE) aims to identify unseen relations between entities in the input sentence. Existing prototype-based methods map sentences and relation prototypes into the same vector space and predict relations by calculating their similarity. However, the performance of these methods is often limited by the quality of sentence and relation prototype representations. To address this issue, we propose a semantic alignment-enhanced framework for zero-shot relation extraction, SAERE. We use large language models to reconstruct the input sentence, reducing interference from redundant context, and insert special tokens into the reconstructed text to highlight the semantic features of the target relation. Additionally, we introduce an adaptive learning mechanism to assign dynamic weights to different features of both the sentence and relation prototype, further improving semantic alignment. We conduct experiments on the FewRel and Wiki-ZSL datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple evaluation metrics.

title: Complementing Self-Consistency with Cross-Model Disagreement for Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often produce confident yet incorrect responses, and uncertainty quantification is one potential solution to more robust usage. Recent works routinely rely on self-consistency to estimate aleatoric uncertainty (AU), yet this proxy collapses when models are overconfident and produce the same incorrect answer across samples. We analyze this regime and show that cross-model semantic disagreement is higher on incorrect answers precisely when AU is low. Motivated by this, we introduce an epistemic uncertainty (EU) term that operates in the black-box access setting: EU uses only generated text from a small, scale-matched ensemble and is computed as the gap between inter-model and intra-model sequence-semantic similarity. We then define total uncertainty (TU) as the sum of AU and EU. In a comprehensive study across five 7-9B instruction-tuned models and ten long-form tasks, TU improves ranking calibration and selective abstention relative to AU, and EU reliably flags confident failures where AU is low. We further characterize when EU is most useful via agreement and complementarity diagnostics.

title: Cognitive Phase Transitions in Semantically Constrained Vector Quantization: Emergent Retrieval/Inference Separation Under Physical Bandwidth Constraints
abstract: We study the emergence of cognitive structure in Vector Quantization (VQ) systems operating under physical bandwidth constraints. Through systematic experimentation on operational maintenance language, we identify a phase transition governed by the ratio N/K (number of training samples to codebook size): below a critical threshold γ_c ≈ 25–30, VQ codebooks spontaneously separate retrieval-type and inference-type communications into distinct Voronoi regions, without explicit supervision. We formalize this as the Cognitive Emergence Law: N/K < C · d_cog, where d_cog measures the intrinsic cognitive separability of the input domain (Cohen's d = 2.45 on raw BPE tokens) and C_emp = 0.391 ≈ 1/e = 0.368 (6.3% deviation explained by mean-field corrections). We show that this emergence is driven by the inputs themselves rather than the reward model — random reward outperforms MiniLM reward (2/3 vs 1/3 seeds significant at K=128, N/K=1.55), confirming that cognitive structure is a property of operational language under compression, not an artifact of supervision. These results have direct implications for bandwidth-constrained AI inference systems (SMS, 2G, LoRa, satellite), where semantic compression must preserve functional distinctions rather than topical similarity. The critical ratio N/K < C · d_cog provides a deployable design parameter for such systems. Preprint. HAL identifier: hal-05596229.
